solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, enumeration length); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's answer wrong at 24 across, corrected here

clue.text: Career detectives knocked back cocktail

indicators.note: a drink knocked back goes down in one; here the letters go backwards

parts.note: to career is to race along

explanation.surface: A police officer's working life has ended with a drink downed in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun for a working life; it is the verb, to rush headlong. RACE + DIS is then read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain example: a sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Outline of comedy routine

explanation.surface: A comedian's rough plan for a new act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' reads as belonging to the phrase, but it only links two separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a sketch is a rough drawing or outline, and a short comic piece.

clue.text: Vicar's attire upset deity, culminating in arrest

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down
the word for arrest comes at the end

parts.note: to collar someone is to arrest them

explanation.surface: A vicar's clothes offend God and end with him being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: A dog collar is the stiff white clerical collar worn by clergy; the surface's upset deity is just GOD read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the stiff white band round a cleric's neck is the garment that marks out a vicar.

clue.text: Auditor's instruction to pay off Russian playwright

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so the words come by ear

parts.note: an instruction to settle something with a cheque

explanation.surface: An accountant tells someone to settle up with a Russian dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant checking the books; it is a hearer. Cheque is the British spelling of check, the bank payment slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Chekhov wrote The Seagull and The Cherry Orchard.

clue.text: Get even with a literate criminal

indicators.note: the letters are treated criminally, i.e. mangled

explanation.surface: Settling scores with an educated crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' seems to be a noun partnered with 'literate'; it is an adjective telling you to rearrange A LITERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to strike back, getting even for a wrong.

clue.text: Before two operations, a large cold drink

parts.note: L = large, as on clothing sizes
C = cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: After two surgeries, a patient wants a big chilled drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold' looks like it describes the drink; it only gives C. An alcopop is a sweet fizzy drink laced with alcohol, sold ready-mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: An alcopop is a drink: a pre-mixed fruity alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: See eye to eye on time limits

parts.note: an age is a period of time
re = on, concerning; it sits inside AGE

explanation.surface: Two people agree about deadlines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On time' reads as punctual, and 'limits' as deadlines; split them apart and 'limits' is the container instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: two people who see eye to eye share the same view.

clue.text: Measure key port to the north of church

indicators.note: in a down clue, above: the port comes before the church

explanation.surface: A tune in some key composed in a harbour town north of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Measure' is the musical or poetic sense: rhythm, beat.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is rhythm or beat, as is measure in verse or music.

clue.text: Father about to relax endlessly in square

indicators.note: the last letter is dropped

parts.note: LAZE without its E, placed inside PA

explanation.surface: Dad goes off to take it easy in the town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' belongs with 'relax' as the infinitive, not a link. 'In' is only the join to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public square, especially in a Spanish-speaking town.

clue.text: Plant from Montana extremely reflective in light

indicators.note: only the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: MT = Montana, the US state abbreviation

explanation.surface: A plant from Montana with shiny, pale leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflective in light' reads as shiny in sunshine, but 'light' is the adjective, meaning pale in colour, and it holds both inserted pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by genus: the palm is a tropical tree, and every tree is a plant.

clue.text: Kitchen item for one consumer east of Great Britain

indicators.note: in an across clue, to the right of, i.e. after

parts.note: one who consumes; placed after GB

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget suited to someone who buys and eats in eastern Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For one' looks like a phrase about suitability; it gives EG, 'for example'. It comes first, even though the clue says 'consumer' is east of GB.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg beater is a hand whisk, a kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Speak slowly to attract learner

explanation.surface: A teacher speaks slowly to draw in a new pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To attract learner' reads as a purpose; it is just DRAW + L side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To drawl is to speak in a slow, drawn-out way.

clue.text: Fool next to source of hazardous material

indicators.note: the two parts sit side by side
a word's source is its first letter

explanation.surface: An idiot stands by a supply of dangerous substances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazardous material' reads as one phrase; 'material' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: material in the dressmaker's sense, woven fabric.

clue.text: Prepare to ambush load for dictator after some extra sleep

indicators.note: a dictator here is one who dictates, speaking words for another to write down

parts.note: a lie-in is a morning spent in bed

indicators.note: the load comes after the sleep

explanation.surface: A tyrant, rested after a long sleep, gets ready to spring a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dictator' conjures a tyrant, but it means someone dictating aloud. A lie-in is the British term for staying in bed late.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to hide ready to ambush someone.

clue.text: Bond offering from heads of legal industry needed vital changes

indicators.note: the letters are changed round
the heads of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letters of Legal and Industry

explanation.surface: A company issues a bond after its lawyers say changes are essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bond' is not a financial bond but James Bond: Live and Let Die is a 1973 Bond film.
explanation.definitionFit: Live and Let Die is one of the James Bond films, an offering in the series.

clue.text: Transport for Arab army with odder tanks

indicators.note: to tank is to crash, so the letters are wrecked

parts.note: anagram fodder; with ARMY, nine letters

explanation.surface: An Arab army's vehicles include some rather strange tanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tanks' looks like military vehicles; it is the verb, to tank (collapse), and tells you to rearrange ARMY and ODDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dromedary is the one-humped camel of Arabia, a traditional beast of transport.

clue.text: Cleaner put off dope with therapy initially

parts.note: to deter is to put off

indicators.note: at the start: only the letter that begins the word is used

explanation.surface: A cleaner is discouraged from drugs by a course of therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like drugs; it is information, the 'gen' (British slang).
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'cleaner' as the substance, not the person, the soap-like product that lifts dirt.

clue.text: Delightful scheme briefly seen on Dynasty

indicators.note: said briefly, the word is cut short and loses its last letter
in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the second

parts.note: CHART, a scheme or plan, without its last letter

explanation.surface: A lovely plan spotted on the 1980s TV soap Dynasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital D dresses 'Dynasty' as the American TV soap; it is the Chinese dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both adjectives describe something that pleases and enchants.

clue.text: Fantastic clue pro to hire?

indicators.note: the letters take a fantastic form

explanation.surface: A superb professional detective available for hire.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: rearrange CLUE PRO TO HIRE, and the result is a fictional private detective who follows clues for a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's fictional detective, a professional reader of clues.

clue.text: Party dumping leader charges to greater heights?

indicators.note: the party loses its first letter

parts.note: DUP, the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland, without its D
wards are people in someone's charge

explanation.surface: A political party gets rid of its leader and its fortunes rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a party leader being ousted, but it is only the first letter of DUP. 'Charges' is people in your care, not fees.
explanation.definitionFit: The question mark flags an adverb given as a phrase: upwards means towards greater heights.

clue.text: Mechanical mug with old idiosyncrasy

parts.note: a tic is a habitual quirk

explanation.surface: A drinking mug with an odd old quirk to its workings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a cup; it is the verb, to rob.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic means mechanical, like a machine.

clue.text: Typhoon at sea shedding variable amount of light

indicators.note: all at sea: confused, so the letters are jumbled
as a tree sheds leaves, the word casts off a letter

parts.note: Y, an algebraic variable, is shed before the rest is rearranged

explanation.surface: A typhoon at sea blots out the sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' fits a typhoon perfectly, but it is the anagram indicator; 'variable' is not an adjective for 'amount' but the letter Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A photon is the smallest quantum of light, a minimal amount of it.

clue.text: Expert follows Frenchman with whiskey never running out

indicators.note: the expert comes after the rest

parts.note: W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A skilled drinker keeps pace with a Frenchman whose whiskey never runs dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whiskey' is not a drink here but Whiskey, the NATO code word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: energy from wind or sun is replenished as it is used, so its supply never runs out.

clue.text: Stocking stuff inside many longboats

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the next words

explanation.surface: Items stuffed inside a fleet of Viking longboats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stocking stuff' reads as filling a Christmas stocking; it is the fabric stockings are made from.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is the material stockings are made from; stockings are even called nylons.

clue.text: What may generate fanfare for top officials

definitions.meaning: the section of trumpets and horns that sounds a fanfare

explanation.surface: A trumpet flourish announcing senior dignitaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' reads as the fanfare being in honour of the officials, but it just links two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Trumpets and horns, the brass, sound fanfares; the brass is also slang for senior officers.

clue.text: Space to sleep on board as back of big gun is removed

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its last letter
that letter is taken away

parts.note: Big Bertha, the huge German howitzer of the First World War

explanation.surface: Room to sleep aboard a warship once the rear gun has been taken out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big gun' is Big Bertha, the German siege gun, so 'big' is part of its name as well as the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A berth is a sleeping bunk on a ship or train.

clue.text: One inactive feature of scoundrel disappointingly making a comeback

indicators.note: the answer is a feature within the words
the letters come back, right to left

parts.note: the last three letters of scoundrel plus the first two of disappointingly, then read right to left

explanation.surface: A layabout rogue fails to stage a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disappointingly' looks like an anagram indicator; it is fodder, supplying DI.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive paraphrase: a person who does nothing, a loafer.

clue.text: Flat feet ultimately observed on separate guys

indicators.note: in the end, so the letter that ends the word
in an across clue, placed after the rest

explanation.surface: Flat-footed men watched from a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat feet' reads as a condition; 'Flat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Apartment is the American word for a British flat.

clue.text: Familial inheritance is beginning

parts.note: what you inherit from your family

explanation.surface: Family heredity is where everything starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' looks like the link between definition and wordplay; it is part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A genesis is an origin or beginning, as in the first book of the Bible.

clue.text: Animal found in capital of China and part of Mexico

indicators.note: the animal is found inside the money

parts.note: the yuan is China's currency, its capital in the money sense

explanation.surface: An animal spotted in Beijing and in southern Mexico.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital of China' wants to be Beijing or the letter C; it is money, the yuan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yucatán is a peninsula and state in south-east Mexico.
